data.name: FirstRunIntro
data.value: Complete the three steps below to keep the hardware service and avoid control conflicts.

data.name: FirstRunStep1Body
data.value: The installer has already set up the GCU service and driver; this program includes all required components. The official console has been cleaned up and replaced by L-Mechrevo, so there is no need to download or install it.

data.name: FirstRunStep2Body
data.value: Open the System page in this program to configure startup, performance mode, GPU mode and lighting; the GCU service runs in the background with no extra steps needed.

data.name: FirstRunStep3Body
data.value: Do not run BetterRGB, OpenRGB or other vendor lighting programs at the same time; multiple programs grabbing HID devices can make lighting fail or cause device access conflicts.

data.name: FirstRunStep4Body
data.value: Look in BIOS or the official console: is there an "iGPU only / integrated-graphics only" option? "Yes" shows the iGPU-only mode button, "No" hides it; "Not sure" keeps it visible, and you can change this any time in Settings.

Turn it off any time in Settings → Privacy & feedback.

data.name: ChargeTaskLocationBody
data.value:
L-Mechrevo is installed in a directory that ordinary users can write to: {0}
Installing into a directory that ordinary (non-administrator) accounts can write to is a security risk: the program files there can be replaced by such an account, so L-Mechrevo refuses to register the charge-limit boot task as SYSTEM (otherwise the swapped-in file would run automatically as SYSTEM at boot - privilege escalation).
Note: the default location C:\Program Files\L-Mechrevo is protected and never shows this prompt. Seeing this prompt means the directory really does allow ordinary-user writes (checked against the access rules of both the directory and the exe).
Consequence: after a full power loss the charge limit will not be restored automatically and may silently revert to 100%. Normal restarts hide the problem.
Tighten this directory's permissions now? (only administrators will be able to write; normal users can still read and run L-Mechrevo)

data.name: ChargeTaskElevationNotice
data.value: Charge-limit restore at boot is not enabled: registering the SYSTEM scheduled task requires administrator rights. Right-click L-Mechrevo and choose "Run as administrator".

data.name: ChargeTaskLocationFixed

data.name: CpuTuneRisk
data.value: Start with small steps. Excessive undervolting or overclocking can freeze or restart the PC. Command acceptance does not prove stability; restore defaults if errors occur.

data.name: CpuTuneScope
data.value: Applies for this boot and is kept when the performance mode changes. Apply writes and saves the value; Save only writes the config (CO and FMax, no SMU command); Load reads the saved CO and FMax back and applies them; Reset zeroes the CO of every core, exits fixed-clock mode and puts FMax back to the baseline read last time (when no baseline was recorded, no FMax value is guessed).

data.name: CpuTuneScopeNonAmd
data.value: This machine exposes no writable CPU tuning interface: FMax (PBO maximum frequency), Curve Optimizer and fixed all-core clock are AMD platform features and are not shown here. Detect only performs a read-only probe and writes no setting.

data.name: CpuTuneSmuReady
data.value: AMD command route detected. Firmware may reject changes. Fixed clock has no independent readback; CO can be read back (it reflects the SMU's current state, not the last value written). Success still only means the SMU accepted the command.

data.name: CpuTuneSmuPartial
data.value: AMD command route detected, but part of it is blocked for this SKU (see the notes below): the locked options stay visible as unavailable, while the remaining writable options are still offered. Fixed clock has no independent readback; CO can be read back (it reflects the SMU's current state, not the last value written). Success still only means the SMU accepted the command.

data.name: CpuTuneUnsupported
data.value: No supported writable interface detected. Hybrid Intel CPU ratio control requires further validation.

data.name: CpuTuneVerified
data.value: Applied; CPU setting readback matches. Stability still requires testing.

data.name: CpuTuneForcedNotice
data.value: Debug switch LMECHREVO_FORCE_CPU_TUNING is on: this window is shown by force, not by capability detection. Apply / Restore still follow the detected capability and stay disabled when no writable interface is found.

data.name: CpuTuneAutoApply

data.name: CpuTuneAutoApplyWarning
data.value: With this on, every startup really writes these settings (not a read-only check; FMax is only written where this machine can write it); it lasts for this boot only and the firmware starts over after a reboot. Leave it off unless you are sure.

data.name: CpuTuneAutoApplyConfirm

data.name: CpuTunePerCoreCodenameOnly
data.value: This codename has no per-core CO write command in the SMU reference, so only the all-core CO write is available (Vermeer is the one codename measured on real hardware).

data.name: CpuTunePerCoreNotCurve
data.value: Per-core CO applies to the all-core Curve Optimizer entry only.

data.name: CpuTunePerCoreBaselineUnknown
data.value: unavailable (no per-core readback on this platform)

data.name: CpuTuneAutoApplyWarningTip
data.value: Details: the write is a real SMU command and the SMU state can be read back afterwards; a bad offset can freeze or restart the PC. The switch only does something on desktop Vermeer (the per-core write path measured on a Ryzen 7 5700X); elsewhere the switch and the buttons stay disabled. Turning it on saves the values currently in the boxes, and those saved values are what a startup replays. The same switch also replays the saved FMax (cpu_fmax_saved) through the existing PBO write path, on machines whose codename has an FMax write command.

data.name: CpuTuneGuardSkipped
data.value: The last shutdown was not clean, so startup auto-apply was skipped this boot (no CO and no FMax value was written). Switch: Custom mode -> CPU tuning.

data.name: CpuTuneGuardSkippedTip
data.value: Windows saw no clean exit last time (crash, power loss or a forced kill), so this start did not write the saved per-core CO values or the saved FMax into the SMU - a possibly unstable setting is not re-applied. To turn the feature off: Custom mode -> CPU tuning -> clear "Apply the saved CO values and FMax at startup". The line disappears after one clean shutdown.
